title: A magnetic monopole in a superfluid bubble
abstract: Magnetic monopoles lie at the crossroads of gauge fields, topology, geometric phases, and charge quantization, yet they remain elusive as fundamental particles. Here we show that an emergent Dirac-monopole framework arises naturally from the dynamics of massive quantum vortices in a spherical superfluid shell. Their dynamics is formally equivalent to that of interacting charged particles constrained to a sphere in the field of a magnetic monopole. The monopole charge is fixed by the superfluid density and automatically satisfies Dirac's quantization condition. The emergent monopole description predicts cyclotron-like vortex motion, in quantitative agreement with Gross--Pitaevskii simulations. We further show that topological frustration induced by two like-charged polar vortices gives rise to the formation of an equatorial vortex necklace, a configuration reminiscent of the polygonal cyclone clusters observed around Jupiter's poles, before its subsequent breakup through a Kelvin--Helmholtz-like instability. Within this framework, the vortex necklace may be viewed as a quantized analogue of Wu--Yang gauge patching. Our results establish spherical superfluids as a versatile platform for realizing and exploring fundamental aspects of Dirac-monopole physics.
summary: The authors demonstrate that the dynamics of vortices in a spherical superfluid naturally generate an effective magnetic monopole field, confirming the system's utility for studying Dirac-monopole physics. They analyze vortex motion analogous to charged particles in this field and further study the instability growth of related vortex structures. This establishes spherical superfluids as a versatile platform for exploring fundamental topological quantum phenomena.
main_problem: To establish a unified framework realizing the Dirac-monopole paradigm using controllable quantum fluid systems, and to study vortex instabilities related to this structure.
main_result: The dynamics of massive vortices in a spherical superfluid naturally generate an effective gauge potential equivalent to that of a magnetic monopole, and the system exhibits predicted cyclotron-like motion and subsequent instability growth rates.
method: The work combines theoretical derivations (effective Lagrangian, normal-mode analysis) with numerical simulations using the Gross-Pitaevskii equation on a spherical geometry.
model_or_system: The physical platform is an immiscible binary Bose–Einstein condensate confined to a thin spherical shell. The model incorporates vortex interactions and derives effective gauge fields leading to monopole dynamics.
key_observables: Cyclotron frequency ($\omega_c$), instability growth rate ($\sigma^*$), superfluid density distributions, and the emergent magnetic field ($B_j$).
important_parameters: Superfluid density ($ho_a, ho_b$), vortex charge quantization ($q_j g = n\hbar/2$), and effective mass ($M_b$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the immiscible regime for the condensate and relies on mapping dynamics to an effective gauge structure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the analogy between vortex dipoles and charged particles in a monopole field, show dipole trajectories, and plot the exponential growth of vortex necklace amplitudes over time.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the monopole emergence from vortex dynamics on a sphere, then analyzes the resulting cyclotron motion via normal modes and GPE simulations. Finally, it investigates the instability of an equatorial vortex necklace configuration related to Wu-Yang gauge patching.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, controllable quantum fluid realization of fundamental topological physics (monopoles), linking superfluid dynamics directly to concepts from high-energy theory like Dirac quantization and geometric phases.
